text:
jen: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands re: capacity/regions/autoscale. Wanted to capture a few Qs we didn't get to live so comms can draft a short customer note.

alex: Shoot the questions. I'll summarize fallback order and ops constraints.

j en: Typo 😅 meant to say: First: what's the canonical fallback order we can share with customers (short bullet)? Second: how do SLAs look if we route cross-region? Third: any public metrics we plan to expose after spikes?

maria: Canonical fallback order (short): 1) in-region prewarmed lane(s) 2) same-region alternate SKU/quantized variant 3) nearest healthy region (latency increase) 4) customerdedicated/reserved pool (if committed) 5) model-family downgrade only if customer opted in.

alex: For routing priorities: capacity_hint -> customer_affinity_flag -> tier/SLO -> latency_budget -> cost_policy. That decides tie-breaks for concurrent pressure.

tia: How long does prewarm take and do we charge for prewarm? Customers worry about warm-up time for big models.

maria: Typical prewarm: 30s-2m depending on SKU and model size. We maintain warm pools for popular models in major regions. Billing: prewarm is covered by reserved capacity credits for committed customers; otherwise prewarm is billed as minimal allocation while warm (small flat fee + compute). We'll add a clear FAQ line.

marco: SLA language: if a request is routed cross-region do we still count against in-region latency SLO? important for enterprise contracts.

rebecca: Short answer: in-region requests served from in-region warm lanes count toward regional latency SLA. Cross-region fallbacks are documented as "best-effort continuity" and not included in strict in-region latency SLOs. We'll provide customers a contract appendix for enterprise customers that need cross-region guarantees (dedicated pools or multi-region reserved options).

alex: Ops note: we try to avoid in-flight model switches. If we must switch families mid-stream we use KV/prefix handoff where compatible, otherwise we do a continuation prompt and mark metadata: `fallback_reason` and `handoff=true`. Clients can inspect those fields.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: region-fallback policy config updated by @maria at 09:12  canary bumped 10% -> 35% during ramp.

jen: Metrics to publish: % requests cross-region, median latency delta for affected requests, top affected regions, and a short timeline for the event. We'll avoid disclosing customer IDs.

marco: Can we schedule a weekly digest for product teams so sales/AE can answer customer questions quickly?

alex: Yes, I'll add a recurring "capacity digest" to the infra mailbox. Will include raw percentages + any action items.

maria: Action items: I'll draft the internal handoff doc + prewarm billing FAQ. rebecca will draft SLA appendix language. alex will produce the digest template. jen will coordinate the short customer note with comms.

rebecca: I'll post the SLA appendix draft in #legal-ops once ready.

jen: Thanks all. If anyone has a customer example where cross-region fallback would be problematic, drop it here and we'll fold into the appendix.

alex: small snippet for docs (feel free to copy):
```
Fallback order: in-region prewarm -> same-region SKU -> nearest region -> reserved pool -> model fallback (opt-in)
Latency policy: in-region served = regional SLA; cross-region = continuity best-effort
```

jen: perfect, thanks. Closing thread unless more input.
